sections.h2: Two tax bills for every Smyrna homeowner
sections.html:
Two governments bill you. Cobb County sends county and school taxes through the Cobb County Tax Commissioner, and the City of Smyrna sends its own separate city bill. Many owners expect one statement and miss the second, so confirm both before you list a house or sign a contract.

The county's tax estimator covers county taxes only, so city residents should contact the municipal tax office for city figures. Smyrna's city tax department sits at City Hall, 2800 King Street. Occupational taxes are collected separately through business license renewals, and the city imposes no municipal sales tax.

For context, Smyrna has an estimated 57,513 residents. Owners occupy 59.4% of homes, the median owner-occupied value is $449,500, median gross rent is $1,739, and median household income is $100,061.

The two bills run on different calendars. Cobb mails its bills by August 15 to the January 1 owner and sets the due date at October 15. Smyrna issues its bills in September and puts the due date in November.

The city mails statements to the homeowner and not to the mortgage company, because loans are sold so often. If your lender pays from escrow, ask whether the servicer also gets the Smyrna city bill.

Smyrna homeowners can ask for exemptions from both governments, and each one is filed with its own office. The city offers these:

  • A homestead exemption for all Smyrna homeowners that caps city tax at the home's initial assessed value, filed once and kept for later years.
  • A $10,000 reduction for owners age 62 or older by January 1, notarized. Notarizing is available at City Hall.
  • A $22,000 reduction for owners who are totally disabled as of January 1, with net income not above $12,000.

Rental properties do not qualify for the city homestead exemptions. City forms are due by April 1 at City Hall, by mail to 2800 King Street, by fax or by upload, and the city tax line is (678) 631-5325.

Cobb County keeps a separate list: a $10,000 basic homestead exemption that carries a $2,000 state component, an age 62 school tax exemption, an age 65 exemption with an income limit of $10,000, and a state tax exemption for owners 65 and older on the home and up to 10 acres. Every qualification must be met as of January 1, and city residents file city exemptions at the city tax office.

sections.h2: How to pay, and what happens if you fall behind
sections.html:
The city accepts payment these ways:

  • Online at smyrnaga.gov, by e-check or card.
  • By phone at 877-765-7651.
  • By mail to Attn: Tax Department, PO Box 1226, Smyrna, GA 30081.
  • In person on the second floor of City Hall.

Online card or debit payments carry a fee of the greater of $2.50 or 3.5%, e-checks carry $1.95, and in-person check or cash payments carry no added fee.

Unpaid bills accrue penalties and interest, and a FIFA lien is recorded with the Cobb County Clerk of Superior Court against the property address and the owner. That lien lets the city collect before a sale can occur. Ask the Smyrna Tax Department for a payoff figure in writing before a closing date is set.

The Cobb County assessment notice carries the appeal deadline, so read the notice for the date. Homestead applications are tied to it too: an application must be postmarked or received before the appeal deadline on the Notice of Assessment, and later applications are processed for the following year.

The Cobb tax commissioner also processes tax sales, mobile homes, boats and aircraft, and prepares the annual tax digest. The assessor's office, a separate office, handles valuation questions and appeals.

sections.h2: How the city tax is calculated
sections.html:
Take the total appraised value, multiply by 40%, subtract exemptions, multiply by the millage rate, and divide by 1,000. Each owner's exemptions differ with eligibility, so two neighbors with the same appraisal can receive different city bills.

The 62 and older exemption, the totally disabled exemption and the floating homestead exemption apply only while the owner lives at the property that receives them. Ask the Smyrna Tax Department what a buyer must file after closing, since the owner's residence is a condition of each exemption.

The county estimator is for a single tax year and is not a bill, so rely on the official bill when you negotiate a credit.

sections.h2: Permits and rental rules before you sell
sections.html:
The city's Building Division requires permits for roofs, windows, decks, interior remodeling, pools, generators, solar panels, demolition and any project with two or more trades. General building permits are $7.00 per $1,000 of construction cost plus a 10% records fee and a $15.00 technology fee, with a $125.00 minimum. Residential plan review typically takes 5 to 10 business days, and all applications go through the online portal.

A homeowner can pull a permit only for a permanent residence listed in the owner's legal name, and a landlord working on a rental must hold a Georgia contractor license. Short-term rental licenses come from the Business License Division, and Code Enforcement handles complaints such as high grass and debris. Call Community Development at (678) 631-5387 about open permits.

The city's parcel search map shows zoning for a given lot, which helps if a buyer plans a particular use.

An unpaid city bill does not stop a sale by itself, but the lien does complicate it. Ask the Smyrna Tax Department for the payoff, ask Cobb for the county balance, and give both figures to your closing attorney. Both come out of your proceeds at the table. A cash buyer can accept a house with a lien as long as title is cleared at closing, which is why owners who are behind on taxes often start with cash offers.

Collect the paperwork first: your deed, the latest Cobb assessment notice, the most recent city bill, and proof of any exemptions you hold. A buyer who plans to live in the house will have to file for their own exemptions, since yours end with your residence.

faqs.q: Does Smyrna have its own property tax?
faqs.a: Yes. The City of Smyrna issues its own bill, separate from the Cobb County bill. City bills go out in September and are due in November, and the city millage rate has been 8.99 mills since fiscal year 2008.

faqs.q: Where do I file a Smyrna city homestead exemption?
faqs.a: File with the City of Smyrna Tax Department by April 1. The city accepts forms by mail to 2800 King Street, by fax at (770) 431-2814, by upload, or in person at City Hall. For questions call (678) 631-5325.

faqs.q: When is the Cobb County property tax bill due for a Smyrna address?
faqs.a: October 15. Cobb mails bills by August 15 to the January 1 owner and requires a U.S. postmark or receipt by the deadline, with metered and kiosk postmarks not accepted. The city's separate bill is due in November.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Smyrna house if the city tax bill is unpaid?
faqs.a: Yes, but the city can record a FIFA lien at the Cobb County Clerk of Superior Court, and that lien lets the city collect before a sale occurs. Get a payoff from the Smyrna Tax Department and have it paid at closing through your closing attorney.

faqs.q: Do rental houses in Smyrna get the city homestead exemption?
faqs.a: No. The city's homestead exemptions apply only to residential property that is the owner's primary residence, and rental properties do not qualify.
